title: The Living Research Book
lines: The Living Research Book proposes a different unit for communicating an evolving research programme.
Its starting point is that scientific work already exceeds the articles describing it.
Claims depend on datasets, code, decisions, failures, and knowledge scattered across separate records.
The distinctive proposal separates evidence records while presenting a coherent, versioned intellectual account.
This is an institutional design to investigate, not a prediction that longer publications automatically improve science.
Readers can examine how maintained knowledge might support explanation, review, credit, and selective disclosure.

title: Research exceeds its report
lines: The book begins with a mismatch between research activity and its conventional public account.
Evidence, code, decisions, and revisions develop across many separate working materials.
An article can describe an important result without preserving every dependency needed for reuse.
Later readers and reviewers must reconstruct connections that the research team once understood.
The proposal asks whether that reconstruction burden can be reduced systematically.
This is why its subject is a maintained research institution, not simply a longer manuscript.

title: Parts underneath, an account above
lines: The book considers a future built from smaller claims, datasets, and executable objects.
Those components support precise reuse but do not automatically provide a coherent explanation.
Its proposal keeps separate evidence records underneath a sustained intellectual account.
Readers could follow the argument while inspecting the dependencies relevant to a particular question.
The monographic form supplies continuity without requiring every detail in one unchanging document.
That combination distinguishes the proposal from both an isolated paper and an unstructured repository.

title: Two meanings of living
lines: A maintained document can change over time without supporting deeper interaction with its contents.
A chatbot can answer questions about a document that never changes.
The book distinguishes these properties instead of treating either as sufficient.
Its living research book would develop with the research and support inspection of its knowledge.
Stable published editions would remain available beside an evolving working account.
The chapter gives readers concrete requirements behind an otherwise easily inflated metaphor.

title: Publication has a boundary
lines: The proposed architecture separates a private workspace, controlled evidence access, and a public book.
It does not call for publishing every internal conversation or confidential research artifact.
Claims and dependencies would inform what a particular edition needs to disclose.
A publication compiler is the proposed process for assembling such an edition.
That name does not remove judgment about interpretation, access, uncertainty, or responsible disclosure.
The book asks readers to examine how explicit boundaries could improve both explanation and restraint.

title: Writing follows the work
lines: The workflow chapters move writing closer to the continuing production of research.
Agents might help maintain links, detect inconsistencies, and prepare views of an evolving project.
Negative results and abandoned decisions could retain value instead of disappearing from the final story.
Human responsibility remains important because a fluent account can still misrepresent the evidence.
Reports and articles become possible views of maintained knowledge rather than its only lasting container.
The reader can evaluate whether these changes reduce repeated work or merely add another maintenance obligation.

title: Review without reconstruction
lines: A reviewer often spends time rebuilding the path between a claim and its support.
The book proposes review materials that expose relevant dependencies more directly.
Controlled access could provide necessary evidence without making all research materials public.
Selective transparency therefore concerns purpose and justified access, not secrecy disguised as rigor.
Continuing review would also need stable versions so criticism targets an identifiable account.
These chapters connect editorial form with the practical work of evaluating a research programme.

title: An institution that might fail
lines: The later chapters imagine changes to credit, careers, maintenance, and institutional incentives.
They also examine fluent but empty accounts, platform dependence, inequality, and maintenance failure.
A more coherent publication can make unsupported claims look more persuasive.
The proposed transition therefore needs tests that measure useful outcomes and the burden imposed.
Small pilots could examine whether reviewers spend less time reconstructing dependencies.
The book leaves room to reject arrangements whose maintenance costs outweigh their contribution.

title: Read the proposed institution
lines: Begin with the mismatch between research work and the record available to others.
Then read the layered knowledge model alongside the boundaries for publication and review.
Keep a real research project in mind when evaluating the proposed workflow.
The limitations and transition chapters are essential parts of the invitation.
The Living Research Book offers an institutional design to question, refine, and test.
Read it to consider what a coherent research account should preserve as knowledge continues changing.
